grammar_focus: 定语从句(who/that,含 the man who…)、what/whatever 引导的名词性从句、since 引导的原因状语从句、if 引导的条件状语从句(含与现在相反的虚拟)、现在分词/形容词作伴随状语(knowing…, glad…)(NCE4 无 KS 页,考点由课文结构自取;IP 最高危:源为伯特兰·罗素极著名散文,其‘个体生命如河流汇入大海’招牌隐喻不复制,已换 100% 原创‘乐曲中一个音符汇入整体和声’隐喻承载同一哲理,只提语法/词表/话题/篇幅;题材=晚年如何看待死亡·平和无害;美语化 realize/honor;第四册第11课)
scene: 有些老人被对死亡的恐惧压得喘不过气。在年轻人身上,这种恐惧尚有道理:一个有充分理由担心自己会英年早逝的年轻人,可以理直气壮地感到痛苦,因为他被夺去了生活所能给予的最好的东西。但在一个活得长久、尝过深切欢乐与沉重悲伤、又做完了命中注定该做的一切工作的人身上,同样的恐惧在我看来就显得凄惨而卑下了。克服它最稳妥的办法是这样:让你的兴趣一点一点地变得更宽广、更超脱个人,直到自我的高墙渐渐后退,你那渺小的一生被纳入某种远为宏大的东西之中。一个人的一生应当像一支长曲里的一个音符。起初,那音符独自响着,焦灼而热切,热情地只歌唱它自己。可随着乐曲展开,别的音符加入进来;它不再作为一个孤单的声音被听见,而成了宏大和声的一部分,最终毫无痛苦地融入整体,不带一丝失落。凡是到了晚年能这样聆听自己一生的人,就不会被死亡的恐惧所压迫,因为他所珍视的事物会在他身后延续下去。而如果随着生命力衰退,疲惫渐渐加深,休息的念头也就不会不受欢迎。就我而言,我愿工作到最后一刻,知道别人会接着做我再也做不了的事,并欣慰地想到:凡是我力所能及的,都确实已经做成。

grammar_card.title: 定语从句 / what 名词从句 / since 原因 / if 条件 / 分词作伴随状语
grammar_card.intro: ①定语从句 who(指人)/ that(指物):a man who has known joys;the things that he cares for。②what/whatever 引导名词从句:what I can no longer do。③since 引导原因:…, since the things will continue。④if 引导条件(可含虚拟 If he were young…)。⑤现在分词/形容词作伴随状语:…, knowing that…；…, glad in the thought that…。

rows: a man who has known joys
what I can no longer do
If weariness increases, rest is welcome
…, knowing that others will carry on

specialRules.rule: 定语从句关系词:指人多用 who,指物用 that/which;作宾语时可省略。
what 引导名词从句时本身在从句里充当成分,相当于 the thing that;不可与 that 互换。
美式拼写:realize(意识到,英式 realise)、honor(荣誉,英式 honour)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What, according to the author, is the best way to overcome the fear of death as you get older?
options: Make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal
Try never to think about death

passage: Some old people are worn down by the fear of death. In the young this dread has a real justification: a young man who has good reason to fear he may be killed before his time can justifiably feel bitter, for he has been robbed of the best that life had to offer. But in someone who has lived long, who has known deep joys and heavy sorrows, and who has finished whatever work it was given him to do, the same fear seems to me abject and ignoble. The surest way to overcome it is this: let your interests grow gradually wider and more impersonal, until, little by little, the walls of the ego begin to recede and your own small life is taken up into something far larger. A single human life should be like one note in a long piece of music. At first the note sounds alone, anxious and eager, singing passionately of itself. But as the music goes on, the note is joined by others; it is no longer heard as one lonely sound but as part of a great harmony, and in the end it fades painlessly into the whole without any sense of loss. Whoever, in old age, can hear his own life in this way will not be oppressed by the fear of death, since the things he has cared for will go on after him. And if, as his vitality decays, weariness gradually increases, the thought of rest will not be unwelcome. For my part, I should wish to keep working to the last, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and glad in the thought that what was possible for me has indeed been done.

stage5.stem: "A young man ___ fears death in battle may feel bitter."(定语从句,指人作主语)
stage5.stem_cn: 害怕死于战场的年轻人可能感到痛苦。

stage5.stem: "The things ___ he has cared for will go on."(定语从句,指物作宾语)
stage5.stem_cn: 他所珍视的事物将会延续。

stage5.stem: "An old man ___ has known joys and sorrows sees death calmly."(定语从句,指人作主语)
stage5.stem_cn: 一位历经悲欢的老人能平静看待死亡。

stage5.stem: "He finished ___ work it was given him to do."(‘无论什么…’引导名词从句)
stage5.stem_cn: 他做完了交给他的一切工作。

stage5.stem: "Others will carry on ___ I can no longer do."(名词从句,‘所…的事’,填关系词)
stage5.stem_cn: 别人会接着做我再也做不了的事。

stage5.stem: "He is glad that ___ was possible has been done."(名词从句作主语,‘所…的’)
stage5.stem_cn: 他欣慰于凡是可能做到的都已做成。

stage5.stem: "He will not fear death, ___ his interests will continue."(‘既然/因为’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他不会惧怕死亡,因为他所关心的事会延续。

stage5.stem: "The old man feels calm, ___ he has done his work."(‘因为’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 老人感到安宁,因为他已完成了自己的工作。

stage5.stem: "___ others will go on after him, he faces death calmly."(句首‘因为’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 因为后人会继续他的事业,他从容面对死亡。

stage5.stem: "___ weariness increases, the thought of rest is welcome."(‘如果’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 如果疲惫加深,休息的念头便受欢迎。

stage5.stem: "The fear fades ___ your interests grow wider."(‘如果/只要’,填连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 只要你的兴趣变得更广,恐惧就会消退。

stage5.stem: "___ he were young, the fear might be justified."(与现在相反的虚拟条件,填条件连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 假如他还年轻,这种恐惧或许还情有可原。

stage5.stem: "He wished to die at work, ___ that others would continue."(现在分词作伴随状语,主动‘知道’)
stage5.stem_cn: 他愿意工作到最后,知道别人会继续下去。

stage5.stem: "She faced the end calmly, ___ in the thought of a full life."(形容词作伴随状语,‘感到欣慰的’)
stage5.stem_cn: 她平静面对结局,欣慰于自己度过了充实的一生。

stage5.stem: "The note sang on, ___ passionately of itself."(现在分词作伴随状语,主动‘歌唱’)
stage5.stem_cn: 那音符继续唱着,热切地歌唱自己。

stage5.stem: "To weigh someone down and trouble them is to ___ them."(“压迫、使烦恼”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 沉重地压着、使某人苦恼。

stage5.stem: "Feeling low, hopeless and miserable is feeling ___."(“凄惨的、卑下的”用哪个词)
"Energy and liveliness of body and mind is ___."(“活力、生命力”用哪个词)
